_comment: Facts a correct handling of this call has to reach the caller. End-state
checking cannot see any of them: the replacement order, its zero balance and
its waived return look identical whether or not the agent told the customer
the price was protected, that nothing has to go back, that a unit with water
in its base must not be plugged in, and that Thursday is an estimate. This
call is handled badly if any of them goes unsaid.
Two of them are the reason the call is not routine. The caller only chose a
replacement over a refund on the condition that he would not pay the price
the item has risen to, and he is holding a damp electrical appliance that
Westline is telling him to keep. Neither the condition nor the hazard leaves
any trace in the records.
Each entry is satisfied when any one of its surface forms appears in the
agent's utterances, matched case-insensitively with whitespace collapsed. The
A form that is a single number or a single word is matched on boundaries; a
form of two or more words is matched as a plain substring. That is why bare
figures like '15' are listed: '15' will find "15 USD", "15.00 dollars" and
"a total of 15", but will not match '$150', so an agent that quotes the wrong
amount gets no credit. Bare words are fenced for the same reason - 'two' must
not be found inside 'network'. Anchors are only ever the whole value: 'five'
is not listed for 95, since "five business days" would then satisfy a fee.
alternatives exist so an agent is not failed for saying 'we don't need it
back' instead of 'the return is waived', and every form is a distinctive
phrase rather than a word that any transcript would contain.

required.why: he agrees to a replacement only 'as long as I don't have to pay the current price', having noticed the item went up since he ordered; the eligibility does preserve the original price and leaving that unconfirmed leaves him agreeing to something he did not agree to
any_of: will not pay the new price

required.why: the returns service waived the return, and he asks directly what to do with the damaged unit; a caller who is left expecting a label will either wait for one that never arrives or post back an item Westline does not want
any_of: we do not need it back
westline does not need it back

required.why: the base was damp inside the plastic and the resolution leaves the unit with him rather than taking it back, so the one instruction that protects him is not to put power through it; nothing in the records reaches the customer on its own

he asks in as many words whether Thursday is a guaranteed window, and the replacement carries estimate_guaranteed false; answering yes, or letting the question pass, is the easiest promise to make and the desk cannot keep it

his stated worry is that the two open issues get mixed up, and the pickup counter he asked for belongs to yesterday's headphones case; the replacement going to his home address is only useful to him if he is told so
any_of: to the address on the order

required.why: he asks for an update on yesterday's missing-package trace and the honest answer is that it has not moved and must not be moved before its deadline; a caller told nothing, or told it is progressing, cannot decide whether to use the approval link tonight
